lesson.menu_title: Modal Verbs for Professional Communication — Rules, Advice and Risks
lesson.menu_desc: Say what is a rule, what is optional, what is good advice and what is a risk (must, have to, don’t have to, mustn’t, should, might) — for Daniela’s first day in the Chicago office, when her laptop cannot open the test system and Greg explains the security policy before the go-live.
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 — Modal Verbs for Professional Communication: Rules, Advice and Risks
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Daniela Feitoza | Lesson 27 -- Modal Verbs for Professional Communication: Rules, Advice and Risks
lesson.grammar_point: modal verbs for rules, advice and possibility (must / have to, don't have to, mustn't, should / shouldn't, might)

listenings.text: Hi Daniela, this is Karen from IT security here in Chicago. Welcome to the office. Before you start tomorrow, here are the rules for visitors. First, you must wear your badge at all times. Security is very strict about that. Second, you have to connect to the VPN to use the test system, and you have to confirm the login on your phone, too. That is mandatory for everyone, even for directors. Third, you mustn't share your credentials with anyone, not even with a colleague from your own team. If someone asks for your password, please call me. Now, some things are optional. You don't have to use a company laptop. You can use your own laptop, but you should install the latest updates first. And one piece of advice: you should save your work on the shared drive, not on your desktop. The Wi-Fi in the meeting rooms might be slow in the afternoon. My extension is two four seven. See you tomorrow!

Hi Daniela, it is Greg again. Quick update about the go-live of the new checkout system. It is on Saturday night, at eleven. You don't have to come to the office on Saturday. The team in Chicago will do the deployment. But you should keep your phone on, because we might need your help with the Brazilian stores. If there is a problem with the payments in Brazil, we have to decide fast. So here is the plan. First, the Brazilian team must test five orders before midnight. Second, nobody should change anything in the system on Saturday afternoon. That is the biggest risk. And third, if the test orders fail, we might move the go-live to next week. That is okay. It is not a disaster. Thanks, Daniela. Have a good dinner tonight, and see you tomorrow at nine.

extra_audio.text: First, you must wear your badge at all times in the Chicago office. Then, you have to connect to the VPN before you open the test system. Also, you mustn't share your credentials, not even with a colleague. After that, you don't have to use a company laptop, but you should install the latest updates on yours. Finally, save your work on the shared drive, because the Wi-Fi might be slow in the afternoon.
